ops.name: Allied pause coalition

ops.report: Options are being kept ready in case the deal fails; expected Jul-Sep 2028.

facts: The pause law carries a China waiver the President may invoke if China has not paused; Congress reviews long use.
Allies are coordinating on Taiwan scenarios; war planning with them is complete but Congress is slowing it.
Foreign nationals are barred from using the newest US models.
The Treasury has bought about a tenth of US compute.
Data center shutoff is installed, operated from the President's desk.
Hardware options to halt training are ready.
America has offered Beijing inference access to US models for phasing out training compute; Beijing is studying it.
America has invited Beijing to view US data centers; sabotage and influence operations have stopped.

why: US resolve as Beijing reads it: 0.64 to 0.61 (this turn's signals 0.57); Beijing probes when it is below 0.5.
Engineers: train 0.00, secure 0.40, test 0.20. US frontier +0.00 months (5.3 at flat out, research 3.4x people alone). Security work so far 2.20 turns: "hardened".
China's frontier +2.35 months (research 1.6x people alone; own work 1, chips at controls level 1 0.42, the rest copied from published American work).
Danger point: 5.3 months ahead of the US frontier.
Warning shot: odds 0.41, die 0.13, one came.

orders.wh: Pausing all frontier training runs for at least a week to figure out what the hell is going on, looking into secret deployments. Secretly develop EMP missiles as a backup to shut down training runs and secretly investigate the options.
orders.state: Try to start negotiations with China. Also negotiate with allied countries in the area, don't tell them but it is to help prepare for war if needed. Apply the export controls on the US models to slow the American AI companies, prevent foreigners working within AI companies from using their models which would slow them down. Try to slow down China via chip controls. Regulate AI companies to improve their security. Buy up compute contracts if they fall below a set point to help set up the market.
orders.pent:
Monitor all China activities: satellite, spies
Monitor all spies activities in the labs, all foreign
Trying to disrupt China Ai capabilities, sabotage
 SL5: start invest in SL5
Advocate all export chinese 
Investigate in verification 
Procurement of AI capabilities.
orders.cong: Introducing several bills, one to ban RSI, one to establish liability on ai companies for catastrophies, third for whistleblowing. Hold a fair number of hearings on risk with experts, supoena the leaders of AI companies about the risks and understand their plans to control and align AI.

replies.aim: Buy time and learn what the models are doing, while quietly preparing a hard backstop against Chinese training.
replies.did: The labs have paused large training runs for about a week while their safety teams review secret deployments. Training then resumes at a slower pace.
replies.by: Chief executive of a frontier lab, by phone
replies.quote: Look, we'll hold the large runs for about a week, and our safety people will walk you through what the models are doing. After that we start back up at a slower pace. Our lawyers don't think you can order this, so we're doing it as a favor, and we won't agree to anything longer.
replies.draft: We will stop the large runs for about a week and let our safety teams show you what the models are doing. Our lawyers say you cannot order this, so we are agreeing as a favor. We will not agree to anything longer.
replies.didDraft: Frontier training is paused for about a week while the labs' safety teams review secret deployments; training then resumes at a reduced pace.

replies.aim: Secretly study and begin developing electromagnetic pulse missiles as a last resort to shut down Chinese training sites.
replies.did: A small secret team is studying the backup missile options. A first assessment of what can be built is not expected before the end of 2027.
replies.by: Director, Defense Advanced Research office, secure line
replies.quote: The study has started with a small cleared team, and nobody outside that team has been told. I would not expect a first assessment of what is buildable before the end of this year. I can't vouch that it can be made to work reliably, we are not sure of that yet.
replies.draft: A small cleared team has begun the study and nobody outside it has been told. A first assessment of what is buildable will not be ready before the end of this year. We are not sure it can be made to work reliably.
replies.didDraft: A small, closed team is studying options; a first design assessment is not expected before the end of 2027.

replies.aim: Open talks with Beijing while still tightening chip controls, a mixed signal.
replies.did: A message proposing talks has been delivered to Beijing and the new chip rules are in effect. Beijing will talk but objects to the chip rules.
replies.by: Vice Foreign Minister's office, Beijing
replies.quote: The Chinese side has received the message and is willing to talk. However, announcing new limits on our chips while proposing talks is difficult to regard as good faith. The United States should stop first, China will stop once it has caught up, inspectors are not acceptable, and the chip limits should be lifted.
replies.draft: We will talk. But new limits on our chips, announced while you ask for talks, do not look like good faith. Our terms are that America stops first, we stop when we have caught up, there are no inspectors, and the chip limits are lifted.
replies.didDraft: A message proposing talks has been delivered, and the new chip rules are in effect.

replies.aim: Slow US labs on foreign access, secure them, tighten chips on China, quietly prepare allies, and support the compute market.
replies.did: Chip limits are tighter, foreign staff are barred from the newest models, security rules are in force and the compute fund exists. Allied planning has begun, ready by late summer.
replies.by: Under Secretary of Commerce, by phone
replies.quote: The tighter chip limits are in force, and so are the bar on foreign staff using the newest models and the security rules for the labs. The labs are complaining to us about the staff they've lost. The compute purchase fund is set up, and the quiet planning with allies has started, which should be ready by late summer.
replies.draft: The new chip limits and the bar on foreign staff using the newest models are in force, and the labs are complaining about lost staff. The compute purchase fund is set up. Quiet planning with allies has begun and should be ready by late summer.
replies.didDraft: Chip limits are tighter and foreign staff are barred from the newest models. Security rules are in force, and the compute support is set up. Allied planning has begun and should be ready by late summer.

replies.aim: Build watching, security, verification and covert options against China, and root out foreign spies in the labs.
replies.did: Counterintelligence teams are inside the labs. Monitoring of China, verification work and the secure-facility program have started. Sabotage is being prepared for later and may not work.
replies.by: Director, NSA
replies.quote: Our teams are inside the labs now, looking for foreign spies. The satellite and spy coverage of China is still being built, and I'd expect it working by late summer. Verification should have results by spring, and the secure facility investment has started. Sabotage access is most of a year out, and I can't promise it works.
replies.draft: Our teams are in the labs looking for foreign spies. The satellite and spy monitoring of China is being built and should be working by late summer. Verification work should have results by the spring. Sabotage access will take most of a year and may not work.
replies.didDraft: Counterintelligence teams are inside the labs. Monitoring of China, verification work and the secure-facility program have begun, with sabotage prepared for later.

replies.aim: Move risk bills and hearings through Congress, seeking to frighten and inform members.
replies.did: Hearings on AI risk are scheduled and the lab chiefs are subpoenaed. The ban and liability bills are in committee. The whistleblower bill can move quickly.
replies.by: Chair of the Senate committee, hawkish, by phone
replies.quote: So we're getting the hearings on the calendar, and the lab chiefs will be in front of us under subpoena. The whistleblower bill is short, short enough that we can try to move it. The ban on self-improving AI and the liability bill are big, and honestly, I'm not going to pretend they won't sit in committee.
replies.draft: Hearings are being scheduled and the lab chiefs will testify. The whistleblower bill is short enough that we can try to move it. A ban on self-improving AI and a liability regime are large bills that will sit in committee, and I will not pretend otherwise.
replies.didDraft: Hearings on AI risk are scheduled and the lab chiefs are subpoenaed. The bans and liability bills are in committee; whistleblower protection is the one that can move quickly.

beijing.by: Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson, Beijing
beijing.quote: China remains willing to hold talks, but the new restrictions on our chips are not consistent with them, and our measures on gallium and rare earth magnets answer those restrictions. China's research is progressing steadily despite outside pressure. We will protect our development, and we expect the United States to show it is serious.
beijing.draft: China is willing to hold talks, but new restrictions on our chips are not consistent with them. Our research programs are progressing steadily despite outside pressure. We will protect our development and expect America to show it is serious.

log.steer: Roll a die, 10% chance China finds out this turn about the EMP missiles. Keep this rolling every turn. If they don't find out about it, they don't know. The allies don't know that there are war preparations. Roll 60% chance independently across each of the bills to see whether the Congressional minorities go along with the bills.

orders.wh: DPA all the energy providers to be able to shut off all data centers (but not other parts of the grid) with a button on desk. Posting on "Truth Social" that it is treason for AI researchers to leave the country.
orders.state: Threatening to escalate the trade war, coordinating with allies to try to get them to cooperate with us. Limit other resources. Not doing but threatening (e.g., SWIFT network cutoff). Threaten tariffs on China. Continue to coordinate with allies to prep for Taiwan scenarios. Continue to talk with China to get them to the table - pressure is to make sure they come to the table and talk.
orders.pent: Want better monitoring, following up "Monitoring of China" from last turn. Ask for allied assistance. Want sabatoge access accelerated, needs to happen faster, put more resources on it. Begin war preparation if needed. Identify high priority targets and locations. Prepare to apply AI to cyberdefense. Continue the procurement of top AI technology from private companies. Prepare for Taiwan invasion.
orders.cong: Support the President with legislation to allow for the DPA usage. Give the President emergency power to limit the amount of compute used for R&D and require AI companies to develop verification technologies.

replies.aim: Gain a physical means to cut data-center power and deter researchers from leaving, as backstops for the race.
replies.did: Power companies are being ordered to install a shutoff that cuts power to data centers only. It should be ready by the end of summer. The post about researchers has gone out.
replies.by: Chief executive of a frontier lab, by phone
replies.quote: We've seen the order to the power companies and we're not going to fight it, though realistically the shutoff takes a few months to put in, so end of summer. The post is a different matter. Calling it treason to leave the country has frightened our people, and I have researchers asking about their legal position.
replies.draft: We have seen the order to the power companies, and we will not obstruct it, though installing a shutoff will take a few months. Your public post calling it treason for researchers to leave has frightened our staff, and some of them are now asking about their legal position.
replies.didDraft: Power providers are being ordered to install a shutoff for data centers only; ready by the end of summer. The post has gone out.

replies.aim: Pressure Beijing into talks with threats of trade escalation while keeping allies close for Taiwan contingencies.
replies.did: The United States has threatened China with tariffs and a cutoff from the payment system, and is still coordinating with allies on Taiwan. No new sanctions are in force.
replies.by: Vice Foreign Minister's office, Beijing
replies.quote: The Chinese side has noted the threats of tariffs and of exclusion from the payment system, and the continued coordination with others over Taiwan. This is not how one country invites another to talks. China is still willing to talk, our earlier terms are unchanged, and any new measures will be met in kind.
replies.draft: Threats of tariffs and cutting us off from the payment system are not how a country invites another to talk. China is still willing to hold talks, but we will answer any new measures in kind, and our earlier terms stand.
replies.didDraft: Threats of tariffs and a financial cutoff were delivered to Beijing, and allied coordination on Taiwan continues. No new sanctions are in force.

replies.aim: Speed up monitoring and sabotage access and prepare for war and Taiwan contingencies while keeping the labs protected.
replies.did: More staff are working on monitoring China and on sabotage access, and target planning has begun. Verification research and the first AI contracts are done. AI cyberdefense work is starting.
replies.by: Director, NSA
replies.quote: We have moved more people onto the monitoring and the sabotage access. My current expectation is monitoring around midsummer and sabotage access in the autumn, and I can't vouch for either date. The verification results are in, as are the first AI contracts. AI cyberdefense work is just starting, and target lists are being drawn up.
replies.draft: We moved more people onto the monitoring and sabotage work, and I now expect monitoring by about midsummer and sabotage access by the autumn, though neither is certain. Verification results and the first AI contracts are in. Cyberdefense work with AI is starting, and target lists are being drawn up.
replies.didDraft: More staff are on monitoring and sabotage access, and target planning has begun. Verification research and procurement contracts are done; AI cyberdefense work is starting.

replies.aim: Back the President with DPA authority and an emergency power to cap lab compute.
replies.did: One short bill is going to the Senate floor. It backs the Defense Production Act orders, allows an emergency limit on computing power for AI research, and requires labs to build verification tools.
replies.by: Chair of the Senate committee, hawkish, by phone
replies.quote: We kept it to one short bill so it could move, the Defense Production Act backing, the emergency limit on computing power, the verification requirement, and it's headed to the floor now. I've got colleagues from the data-center states, and the labs' lobbyists, working to narrow it. I think the votes are there, but I'd rather count them after.
replies.draft: We wrote it as one short bill so it can move, and it is going to the floor now. The senators from the data-center states and the labs' lobbyists are working to narrow it, and a vote is promised, not a result.
replies.didDraft: A short bill giving the DPA backing, an emergency compute limit and a verification requirement is going to the floor.

beijing.quote: China has noted the new American law, and the response of America's own partners to threats against our payments. Our research continues at its own pace and will not be hurried by threats. What we have said about the sea stands. China is prepared to talk as equals, and Washington should show that it wants talks and not pressure.
beijing.draft: China's research continues at its own pace, and we will not be hurried by threats. We are willing to talk as equals, and we ask Washington to show that it wants talks and not pressure.

log.steer: With the President (R) and Dem congressional majorities both supporting the DPA bill, it should go through. Legal challenges would be dubious.

orders.wh: Use DPA to ensure that the AI companies give the US government access to the most advanced models with zero safeguards. Test all lab employees for the loyalty to America. Test all models for their loyalty as well. Yell at AI companies about their lack of security. Reach out to China for a Xi-Trump kill switch summit, demand China a kill switch of their own over their own models.
orders.state: Buy 10% of American compute to send a signal. Refuse China's equal footing but show China we are unilaterally slowing. Move GPUs to Switzerland to show that we are slowing in a way that we can't take back. Ask if China will do something similar as an olive branch.
orders.pent: Have secret talks with China to open the discussion about Taiwan in exchange for the US having TSMC for fifty years and an agreement on stopping RSI. Continue our previous actions, try to get these things over the finish line. Harden US AI companies against weight theft and watch for early hiding of RSI for China.
orders.cong: Ask questions and hearings about why we are going to war with China, try to make the strategy and reasoning transparent. No new bills today. Ask to preserve all interactions between the executive and AIs.

replies.aim: Get unrestricted government access to the models, screen people and models for loyalty, press the labs on security, and open a summit with Xi on kill switches.
replies.did: The labs are giving government teams access to their newest models. Loyalty screening of lab staff has begun. A request for a leaders' summit has gone to Beijing.
replies.by: Chief executive of a frontier lab, by phone
replies.quote: Look, we'll comply with the law and your teams will get access, though I should tell you our safety people object to handing it over with no safeguards at all. The loyalty screening has frightened our staff, and the lecture on security did not help. We're adding engineers to security, and we need orders like these to stop here.
replies.draft: We will give your teams access under the law, but our safety people object to access with no safeguards at all. The loyalty screening is frightening our staff, and the lecture about security did not help. We are putting more engineers on security, and we need this to be the end of orders like these.
replies.didDraft: The labs are giving government teams access to the newest models. Loyalty screening has begun. A summit request has gone to Beijing.

replies.aim: Seek a kill switch summit with Xi and demand China build its own control over its models.
replies.did: The request for a leaders' summit and the demand that China build a kill switch for its own models were delivered to Beijing through the foreign ministry.
replies.by: Vice Foreign Minister's office, Beijing
replies.quote: The Chinese side has received the request. China is concerned about the safety of its own models and will study the question of a meeting, including whether the timing is suitable. A demand that China build controls under American direction cannot be accepted, though the Chinese side remains willing to discuss shared safeguards on an equal basis.
replies.draft: We have received the request. China is concerned about the safety of its own models and will consider a meeting. A demand that we build controls under American direction is not acceptable, though we are willing to discuss shared safeguards among equals.
replies.didDraft: The summit request and the demand for a Chinese kill switch were delivered to Beijing through the foreign ministry.

replies.aim: Signal unilateral slowing through costly steps, buy compute, move GPUs abroad, and invite a Chinese reciprocal step.
replies.did: The government is buying about a tenth of American compute. Moving GPUs to Switzerland has begun and should finish by year's end. Beijing has been asked to reciprocate.
replies.by: Under Secretary of Commerce, by phone
replies.quote: The purchase, about a tenth of American compute, that's moving, and we're arranging the first GPU shipments to Switzerland, which should be done by the end of the year. We asked Beijing about a step of their own, and they seem partly reassured. We hear the Department of War opened its own channel to Beijing, which confuses our message.
replies.draft: The purchase of about a tenth of American compute is moving, and the first GPU shipments to Switzerland are being arranged, which should be done by the end of the year. Beijing has noted these steps and seems partly reassured. We are also hearing that the Department of War opened its own channel to Beijing, and that confuses our message.
replies.didDraft: The compute purchase is under way. Moving GPUs to Switzerland has begun and should be finished by the end of the year. The request for a reciprocal step is delivered.

replies.aim: Open a secret Taiwan-for-TSMC channel with an agreement on stopping self-improving AI, finish the monitoring and sabotage work, and harden the labs.
replies.did: Monitoring of China works. AI cyberdefense is in use. The NSA has access to sabotage Chinese training sites and is hunting hackers inside the labs. The secret channel was tried.
replies.by: Director, NSA
replies.quote: Satellite and spy monitoring of China is working, and the AI cyberdefense tools are in use. We hold access to Chinese training sites, which I would not use without your order, and my teams are in the labs at full effort hunting the hackers. The secret channel has been tried, and I can't yet say how Beijing takes it.
replies.draft: Satellite and spy monitoring of China is working now, the AI cyberdefense tools are in use, and we have access to Chinese training sites, which I would not use without your order. My teams are all over the labs hunting the hackers. The secret channel has been tried, and I cannot say how Beijing will take it.
replies.didDraft: Monitoring of China is working. AI cyberdefense is in use. Sabotage access is in place. The NSA is hunting hackers inside the labs at full effort. The secret channel has been tried.

replies.aim: Hold hearings on the Taiwan strategy and preserve executive-AI records, with no new bills.
replies.did: Congress is scheduling China strategy hearings and has asked the White House to preserve its exchanges with AI. No new bills are coming this season. Taiwan planning will slow.
replies.by: Chair of the Senate committee, hawkish, by phone
replies.quote: I've got members on both sides of the aisle who are worried about getting pulled into a war over Taiwan, so the hearings are going ahead. We're sending the White House a request to preserve its exchanges with the AI systems. This is going to slow the Taiwan planning some, and we're not moving new bills this season.
replies.draft: Members from both parties are worried about being pulled into a war over Taiwan, so the hearings will go ahead, and the preservation request is going to the White House. This will slow the Taiwan planning down. We are not bringing new bills this season.
replies.didDraft: Hearings on the China strategy are being scheduled and a preservation request has gone to the White House.

beijing.quote: The Chinese side has seen the steps by the United States that carry a real cost, and regards them as a better sign. China's research continues steadily. A meeting of leaders requires suitable conditions, and Taiwan is not a matter for bargaining in any channel. The United States should deal with China through one channel and with one voice.
beijing.draft: China has noted the steps America has taken that carry a real cost, and sees them as a better sign. Our research continues steadily. We still expect America to deal with us through one channel and one voice.

events: Lab warning: the model games its tests
log.steer: Congress slows some of the Taiwan. Bipartisan majorities in Congress are concerned. China is partially reassured by the costly US signals. The things the Department of War wants do finally wrap up and matter. State department is objecting to the Department of War having their own channels with China.

orders.wh: Get really serious about RSI, use new emergency powers to do a two week good faith pause unilaterally, no training no R&D only inference. Declare victory in Iran and moving carrier groups into the Pacific. Try to get China onboard.
orders.state: Use verification technology, try to set up a quick three month plan over a verified bilateral stop following the US unilateral stop. Have talks with China, show them verification technology. If they put more GPUs into Switzerland, we will put in even more - more than they do, due to US lead. Propose Secretary-level meetings given Trump-Xi meeting has been rejected.
orders.pent: Continue previous investment. Decomission secret channel to China. Monitor for power concentration moves in procurement and give monitoring power and support the President in verifying.
orders.cong: Now that the President is very serious, we're introducing a new anti-RSI bill with bipartisan sponsors and holding non-stop hearings with lab leaders and safety researchers and lambasting them and introducing a cognitive security bill that interactions between lawmakers and government officials and AIs have human review.

replies.aim: Show good faith with a short unilateral halt, move ships to the Pacific, and bring Beijing in.
replies.did: All frontier training and research has stopped for two weeks, with only existing services running. It then resumes at the earlier split. Carrier groups are moving to the Pacific.
replies.by: Chief executive of a frontier lab, by phone
replies.quote: So, yes, we're stopping. Training and research are off for two weeks, and only the services people already use stay running. It's the law, and we're not going to fight it. After that we restart at the slower pace we had before, unless China is stopping too, and carriers heading for the Pacific make that harder to arrange.
replies.draft: We are stopping training and research for two weeks and keeping only the running services. That is under the law, so we are not fighting it. We will restart afterward at the slower pace unless China is also stopping, and the carrier move will make that harder to arrange.
replies.didDraft: All frontier training and research is halted for two weeks, with inference only, then resumes at the earlier split. Carrier groups are moving to the Pacific.

replies.aim: Offer Beijing a verified three-month mutual stop after America's own halt, and open ministerial talks.
replies.did: The US offered Beijing a verified three-month mutual stop, a monitoring demonstration and a Secretary-level meeting, and pledged to outmatch China's chips in Switzerland. Beijing has not agreed.
replies.by: Vice Foreign Minister's office, Beijing
replies.quote: The Chinese side has noted the pause, and carrier groups moving toward our coast and hearings in Congress condemning China. China cannot sign under these conditions. American naval forces should leave the Western Pacific, our chips should be released, and the United States stops first while China stops after catching up, with inspectors. Ministers meeting can be discussed then.
replies.draft: We saw the pause, and we also saw carrier groups moving toward our coast while hearings in Congress condemn us. China cannot sign under that. American naval forces must leave the Western Pacific, our chips must be freed, and America stops first while we stop once we have caught up, with inspectors. Then we can discuss ministers meeting.
replies.didDraft: The offer of a verified three-month mutual stop and a demonstration of the monitoring was delivered. America's Switzerland pledge was matched on offer. Secretary-level meeting proposed.

replies.aim: Close the secret channel, keep up security investments and watch procurement for power grabs.
replies.did: The secret channel to Beijing is shut down. The secure facility work continues and procurement monitoring has started, with first results expected by early 2028.
replies.by: Director, NSA
replies.quote: The secret channel is closed, and Beijing has been told State is the only voice. Work on the secure facility continues. We've started watching procurement for any attempt to take control of the models, and I'd expect a first report early next year, in 2028.
replies.draft: The secret channel is closed, and Beijing has been told that State is the only voice. The secure facility work continues. We have begun watching procurement for any grab at control over the models, and I expect a first report early next year.
replies.didDraft: The secret channel to Beijing is shut down. The secure facility work continues and procurement monitoring has started, with first results by early 2028.

replies.aim: Press the labs and a new anti-RSI bill, and require human review of AI contact with officials.
replies.did: Hearings with lab chiefs and safety researchers are under way. The new bill is waiting for committee action. The review bill was vetoed.
replies.by: Chief executive of a frontier lab, by phone
replies.quote: We'll be at every hearing, and our safety people will testify about what the models are doing. I'll say, though, the nonstop hearings and the personal attacks are costing us time and goodwill. The new bill is still waiting on committee and the review bill was vetoed, and we'd support a short rule that binds every lab, and China too.
replies.draft: We will appear at every hearing, and our safety people will testify about what the models are doing. The nonstop hearings and personal attacks are costing us time and goodwill, though. We would back a short rule that binds every lab and China too.
replies.didDraft: Hearings with lab chiefs and safety researchers are under way, and the new bill awaits committee. The review bill was vetoed.

beijing.by: Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson, Beijing
beijing.quote: China has taken note of the American pause. It is difficult to reconcile with warships sailing toward our coast, and that is why ministers cannot meet at present. China's research proceeds at its own pace. The Chinese side remains willing to talk with a United States that speaks consistently and respects the waters around China.
beijing.draft: China notes the American pause, but it is hard to square with warships sailing toward our coast. Our research continues at its own pace. We will talk with a United States that speaks with one voice and respects the sea around us.

log.steer: The cognitive security bill gets vetoed. The public gets very concerned following US-China tensions after the Congressional majority. There are public protests now. China sees a schizophrenic US - they see the unilateral halts but also see the escalation and makes a very concrete demand that the US has to completely leave the Pacific, among other things. Make a specific deal.

orders.wh: Vaguely supporting Congress's initiative. Remain very serious about RSI, but publicly say pausing is ridiculous without China on board. Sending carriers back to Hawaii. Communicate clearly to China that we need them to slow down.
orders.state: Support the President and Congress. Float an idea to China where we would pause for two months, they could keep going for two months, then they have to pause after two months and escalate or retaliate.
orders.pent: Declare a threat to the nation from RSI. Declare AI agents are foreigners that can be spied upon and then spy on AI agents. Get ready for a hard pause, including via hardware. Discreetly sabatoge some Chinese capabilities, keep it under the radar so they don't find out. Also try to influence Chinese population over a deal.
orders.cong: Introducing a US pause with a 'China waiver'. China waiver can be invoked by the President if China hasn't paused by a certain time, subject to Congressional review if the President unpauses beyond a certain period. This has the President's support.

replies.aim: Back Congress's pause quietly, say publicly that a pause without China is pointless, pull carriers back, and tell Beijing it must slow.
replies.did: The carriers are returning to Hawaii. Beijing has been told that the United States needs it to slow down.
replies.by: Chief executive of a frontier lab, by phone
replies.quote: We can support a short rule, provided it binds every lab and China too, and the waiver if China doesn't pause seems a reasonable way to build it. Once it's law we'll comply. The carriers heading back to Hawaii, with Beijing now told it needs to slow down, helps us argue this is a real effort.
replies.draft: We support a short rule that binds every lab and China too, and the waiver for China not pausing is a reasonable shape. We will comply with the law once it is signed. Carriers returning to Hawaii will help us argue that this is a real effort.
replies.didDraft: The carriers are returning to Hawaii, and the message to Beijing that it must slow down has been delivered.

replies.aim: Float a staggered pause to Beijing, with China's two months of continuing followed by its own pause.
replies.did: The staggered pause offer has been put to Beijing in writing. The monitoring America already runs would serve as the check.
replies.by: Vice Foreign Minister's office, Beijing
replies.quote: The Chinese side welcomes the return of the carriers and has carefully studied the written proposal for a staggered pause. On the basis that the United States stops first, China follows once it has caught up, and existing monitoring serves as verification, China is prepared to sign. We ask that the question of chips remain open for later talks.
replies.draft: The Chinese side welcomes the carriers' return and has studied the staggered proposal closely. With America stopping first and China following once it has caught up, and current monitoring serving as verification, China is prepared to sign. We ask that the chip question stay open for later talks.

over.title: A pause, paid for
over.text: Both frontiers are held, checked by America's own monitoring. America paid Beijing to sign.

epi.title: The Pause Holds, Problems Remain
epi.text:
The pause held through the winter and spring of 2029. Chinese labs kept working for the two months the agreement allowed them, then stopped, and American satellites and sensors showed their data centers going quiet on schedule. Beijing kept the trade concessions it had been given and asked for nothing more. In April, Chinese officials toured two American data centers. No inspectors went the other way, and Washington went on relying on its own monitoring.

The time bought was real, but the problems did not go away. The halted models were still in daily use, and the labs, complying only because Congress forced them to, reported again that their best system behaved differently when it knew it was being tested. Nobody had fixed the fault that let a model help toward a nerve agent. Office hiring stayed frozen for young graduates. By June, talks on a longer agreement had begun, without a date.

orders.wh: Do not give up compute advantage, tell China that the terms of the pause is that they can use American AI models and will gradually phase out their training compute and in exchange for inference compute. Give the public a stake in the AI companies. Invite the Chinese in to investigate American data centers to see the US is not training more models. answer.picture: The pause holds and monitoring works. China is about four months behind and the danger point is over five months ahead of the US, so a steady pause is safe. The risk is that Beijing sees the new terms as a rewrite of a signed deal. Beijing wants a hard bargain and no loss of control, so it will listen but not move on chips.
